name: a-swiped-space-stays-switched
description:
A horizontal trackpad swipe moves to the next workspace, and it STAYS there. The regression this pins had the rail return to the space it came from a moment later.

The cause is an off-by-one across the surface boundary. A committed swipe reports its SPACE, and the browser answers by asking the page to glide to that space - but the rail counts panes, and Overview holds pane 0. A space passed through unchanged glides one space back, and the rail arriving there reports THAT space, which switches the browser back for real.

So both assertions carry weight in the same run. '0 -> 1' proves the swipe committed; the absence of '1 -> 0' proves nothing undid it. On the broken build the second line appears, because the wrong-way glide announces the space it landed on.

The direction is not free. Swiping backward instead would put the broken glide on Overview, which is not a space and reports nothing, so the absence check would pass on the very build it exists to catch. Forward is the only direction where the regression leaves a trace.

actions.note: an ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost, so the gesture would land in Finder

space-dots-stay-pinned's gesture, copied rather than invented - that scenario commits a swipe 6 runs out of 6. The sign is measured, not reasoned: dx=+45 logs 'dir -1 from 1 to 0', so positive travels toward Overview and this needs the other way.
far longer than any push this surface makes. The regression undid the switch AFTER it landed, so a short settle would have passed throughout it.

assertions.label: the-switch-happened-and-names-both-ends
assertions.note: both ends, so a run that never left the first space cannot satisfy it

assertions.label: it-did-not-come-back
assertions.note: THE ASSERTION THIS SCENARIO EXISTS FOR. The regression showed as a return trip, and a return trip logs its own line. Paired with the arrival above, so it cannot pass by nothing having happened.
the visible tint really is the other space's at the end, not merely logged as such
